summary:
# NOTES: *The Starvel Hollow Tragedy* (Freeman Wills Crofts; single book, 20 chapters + Conclusion)

## Cast
- **Ruth Averill**: ~20, orphan, dark, small, pretty. Niece of Simon Averill. Father Theodore Averill (Bayonne wine merchant, d. 8 Sep 1910). Mother Anne de Condillac (m. Biarritz 24 Jun 1905; d. 17 Jul 1906 giving birth to Ruth; baptised Biarritz 19 Aug 1906). Came to Starvel aged 4. Boarding school in Leeds. Loves Whymper.
- **Simon Averill**: miser, invalid, heart trouble. Hoards notes and gold in safe at Starvel. Dies in fire.
- **John Roper**: attendant/manservant, Scotch (Fife), squint, sneering, sharp tongue. Ex-male nurse, Ransome Institute, Kintilloch. Blackmailed Philpot. Murdered by Philpot.
- **Flora Roper** (née Macfarlane): Roper's wife; former Philpot maid, Roper's lover; murdered by Philpot.
- **Pierce Whymper**: junior assistant, church architects (Nixon & Arbuthnot, Leeds); clerk of works at Thirsby church. Son of Stephen Whymper, Leeds surgeon. Lodgings 12 Stanhope Terrace. Address Oaklands, Bolton Road, Leeds.
- **Markham Giles**: entomologist, ex-soldier (gassed, wounded), heart disease, cottage half mile from Starvel. Dies Tue 14 Sep 1926 (per coffin plate: "died 14th September, 1926, aged 36"). Murdered by cocaine injection.
- **Mrs Oxley / Arthur Oxley**: Thirsby solicitor (managed Averill's affairs); kindly, jovial.
- **Tarkington**: Northern Shires Bank manager, Thirsby; thin, hawk-like. **Bloxham**: his clerk, sardonic face, carried money to Starvel.
- **Sergeant Kent**: Thirsby police, bumptious, "bungling".
- **Dr Emerson**: old Thirsby doctor, retired in all but name; certified Giles's death as myocarditis.
- **Dr Herbert Philpot**: Thirsby doctor (since ~1921). Born 1887; Edinburgh Univ. 1909; Ransome Institute Kintilloch 1913–21. Married Edna Menzies May 1914. Gambler, bankrupt. Murderer.
- **Edna Philpot**: killed 15 May 1921 at Braeside, Kintilloch.
- **Dr Lonsdale**: coroner (stout, walrus moustache).
- **Major Valentine**: Chief Constable, Leeds.
- **Chief Inspector Mitchell**: Yard superior, shrewd.
- **Inspector Joseph French**: Yard, zealous, pleasant, cautious, vain about promotion; wife at home; uses despatch case of apparatus.
- **Inspector Willis**, **Inspector Marshall** (Whitechapel), **Inspector Tanner** (impersonates Munce), **Sergeant Elliott**, **Sergeant Carter**, **Constable Sheldrake**, **Constable Hughes** (shadows Whymper).
- Others: Peter Spence (baker, Hinkston's), Abel Hesketh (town officer), James Stokes (tramp), Mrs Eliza Steele, Misses Julia & Elmina Locke, Judith Carr (barmaid, Thirsdale Arms), George Mellowes (red-haired farmer, Ivybridge), Mrs Palmer-Gore (York, Oakdene, Ashton Drive), Mr Stackpool (vicar), Mr Boyd (sexton, Thirsby church), Colonel Followes (magistrate), Dr Ferguson (Kintilloch), Sergeant MacGregor (Kintilloch), Mr Stephenson (Carter & Stephenson, safe makers, Leeds, safe no. 12,473), Dr Lingard (Hellifield police surgeon), Dr Laming (Home Office), Mr Pullar (Thirsby shoe shop), Mr Simkins (undertaker), Mr Alderdice (Strand jeweller), Stanley and Russell (salesmen), Mr Dashwood and Mr Munce (Dashwood & Munce, stockbrokers, Dover House, Gracechurch St).
- Foreign: M. Prosper Giraud and Mme Madeleine Blancquart (Talloires; fictitious, Whymper's story).

## Ch 1 The Tragedy
- Starvel: dilapidated house in saucer-shaped hollow on moor; Scotch firs; Yorkshire. Roper and wife attend; Ruth dislikes them.
- Ruth met Whymper (church clerk of works at Thirsby); tea at Starvel; moor walks. Love unspoken.
- 10 Sep letter, "Oakdene," York, from Helen Palmer-Gore: invites Ruth for flower show (Wednesday); "Yours very sincerely." Simon gives £10 via Roper. Roper advises not to disturb Simon.
- Next morning (Friday 11 Sep): Simon ill; Dr Philpot laid up with influenza; Dr Emerson old. Ruth and Mrs Roper visit Giles (Giles very weak).
- Thirsby: Mrs Oxley meets Ruth; church with Whymper; Whymper walks her to train.
- York: Mrs Palmer-Gore (large, kindly, moist kisses). Telegram after 2 days: "Terrible accident at Starvel. Your uncle injured. Return Thirsby and stay night with us." Signed "Oxley."
- Baker Spence (Thursday ~11am, 15 Sep) saw roof gone; walls, smouldering. Three bodies presumed: Simon, John and Flora Roper. Roper bodies at NW end; Simon in S wing.
- Ruth visits ruins; grief. Passing funeral of Markham Giles (died Tuesday); vicar Stackpool and Dr Emerson.
- Evening: three bodies found.

## Ch 2 The Inquest
- Mrs Oxley brings breakfast; reveals Oxley drew Simon's will; "some money" for Ruth. Whymper called the evening before.
- Sergeant Kent warns Ruth of inquest. Courthouse, 3 pm.
- Witnesses: Spence; Abel Hesketh (fire-brigade chief; safe found in S wing, opened by Hellifield expert: £1952 sovereigns + burnt papers); Kent (glow seen by tramp James Stokes at Low Tolworth ~4am; Mrs Steele; Misses Locke).
- Ruth: uncle's bed in S wing, Ropers' in W; smelled whisky on Roper; Simon teetotal; ten pounds.
- Dr Emerson: bodies by build (tall slight man = Simon; medium man/woman = Ropers).
- Judith Carr: Roper took small Scotch ~7pm at Thirsdale Arms.
- George Mellowes: drove Roper from Thirsby ~7pm; set down at Starvel gate; close to 8pm, no fire.
- Coroner: Roper's drink not linked to fire; verdict: Simon Ralph Averill, John Roper, Flora Roper died in fire, 15 Sep, cause unknown.

## Ch 3 Mr Tarkington Develops a Theory
- Oxley tells Ruth: estate ~£30–40k, mostly notes in safe; £500 in bank; notes burnt. Ruth's capital ~£2400: invest, £130 pa; £100 for secretarial course London.
- Whymper cold/embarrassed; Ruth stays at Oxleys'.
- Mid-Oct: Tarkington tells Oxley: income ~£1600–1700 (pension £300, annuity £150, Leeds property life interest). Current account; £20 notes sent via Bloxham. Cheque £346; 16 notes (£320) sent ~a week before fire. Numbers recorded.
- Note with number paid in London (Oct). Tarkington's theory: burglars (gang active), Roper surprised; fire to hide. Safe fireproof (Tarkington's view). Ten pounds to Ruth not from safe.
- Oxley urges telling Chief Constable Major Valentine (not Kent). Junior Services Club, Leeds. Valentine letter: safe fireproof; he applied to Scotland Yard.

## Ch 4 Inspector French Goes North
- Chief Inspector Mitchell assigns French: "mare's nest" possible. Suspected murder, robbery, arson. Thirsby; Thirsdale Arms.
- Sergeant Kent: safe maker Carter & Stephenson, no. 12,473 (Leeds), "best fireproof of its day."
- Landlord gossip: Whymper (Ruth affair), Tarkington, Oxley, Emerson, Philpot (gambler, ruinous), Roper (squint, close, sly), Kent a fool.
- Sunday: French at ruins; safe; burnt newspaper flakes (no notes). Fragment: "—ing as we—" / "RAT-CATCHER'S F——".
- Oxley: paper = *Leeds Mercury*. Mercury 14 Sep: "RAT-CATCHER'S FATAL FALL." French found 8 of 11 fragments; papers from 13, 14, 15 Sep.
- Stephenson: papers couldn't burn with door shut; burned while door open.
- French's conclusions: notes removed before fire; newspapers substituted; burned while door open; safe locked after.

## Ch 5 French Picks Up a Clue
- Tarkington: records of 193 twenties from 11 consignments (£3860), from Bloxham's old notebook.
- Bloxham: saw safe 3 times; ~1500 notes (~£30,000); cardboard box of sovereigns.
- Northern Shires Bank HQ, Throgmorton Avenue. Cook's office, Regent Street: 17 twenties in deposit, messenger "strong in twenties."
- Cook's receipts; French searched books. Hit: "Oct. 6th. Pierce Whymper, Oaklands, Bolton Road, Leeds, £16 8s 4d."
- Whymper's letter 18 Sep: second class return London–Talloires, near Annecy, Savoy; passport query. Tickets for 6 Oct.
- Whymper's lodgings (12 Stanhope Terrace). Interview: Whymper lies (note from father). Denies being at Starvel. Admits meeting Roper outside church ~5:30 pm 15 Sep; admits Ruth at station day before fire.
- Constable Sheldrake (with a girl): ~9:30–10 pm 15 Sep, Whymper coming from Starvel lane, face horrified.
- French searches Whymper's desk (Stanhope Terrace; landlady): 24 twenties, £480 in envelope. All numbers on Tarkington's list.

## Ch 6 Talloires, Lac D'Annecy
- Whymper's false statement exposed. French sends constable Hughes to shadow Whymper.
- Sexton: Roper spoke to Whymper outside church gate ~5:30 pm, "delivering message," sober.
- Warrant obtained from Colonel Followes. Vestry room confession: Roper's message ("Mr Averill wants to see you"); visit ~8 pm; Roper gives bulky envelope: 25 twenties (£500) plus letter (in Averill's hand per Whymper); mission to France; left ~9:30.
- Whymper refuses secret; French: "No jury..."; kept under supervision; told to surrender note and notes; handed over note.
- Mitchell: "Another trip to the Continent, eh, French?"
- Paris (Gare de Lyon), 8:10 express, Aix change, Annecy. Hotel Splendide (Whymper 8–11 Oct).
- Talloires monastery-hotel: Whymper asked for M. Prosper Giraud and Mme Madeleine Blancquart; offered 5000 francs reward; police at Talloires and Annecy confirm. French believes story: secret about Ruth's parentage.

## Ch 7 Posthumous Evidence
- Kent sends letter to "Heirs or Assigns of late Mr John Roper" from Metropolitan Safe Deposit Co, King William Street, City (rent 30/- due).
- Safe-box contains envelope: confession dated 15 May 1921, Herbert Philpot, "under compulsion" (intrigue with nurse; attempted murder of wife by accident; killed with cricket bat on temple).
- Kintilloch: *Scotsman* 17 May 1921 "Tragic Death of a Doctor's Wife": Edna Philpot fell down stairs.
- French's letter (5 Nov, from Charing Cross Hotel) to Philpot re "Henry Fuller" gardener; reply: no such man.
- Expert: confession a forgery (shaky, slow). Mitchell: sends French to Scotland.
- Edinburgh; Cupar superintendent: suspicion (Philpots' bad relations; nurse; lunch in Edinburgh hotel); no suspicious circumstances found in 1921 inquiry; Braeside; cook/maid Flora Macfarlane (married Roper ~a month after Mrs Philpot's death).
- Braeside accident: basement stairs, 16-step lower flight; carpet hole. Dr Ferguson.
- Sergeant MacGregor: Roper dismissed from Ransome for trouble; applied for Brazil passport, brother in Santos. Roper and Philpot close at Ransome.
- Ferguson: Roper dismissed for giving drugs to patients twice.
- French gets Roper's old forms for handwriting study. Train to Thirsby via Carlisle, Hellifield.

## Ch 8 Dr Philpot's Story
- Philpot's house at High Street end, Thirsby. Consulting hours 6–8 pm.
- French: "accused of murdering your wife, Edna Philpot, at Braeside ... 15 May 1921 ... cricket bat."
- Philpot's account: Roper caught him with a nurse (in Ransome shrubbery; Roper earlier found Nurse Williams in arms of another? — Roper mentions Nurse Williams as a good nurse protected); Roper demanded 10s/week; Philpot forced written confession (2 Oct 1920, nurse "So-and-so"). Wife's hostility. Roper then: after wife's death, blackmail £2/week; forged confession shown (photo copies). Philpot paid. Moved to Thirsby, Simon Averill called him. Roper applied for job at Starvel through Philpot (~15–16 months before fire). Roper said he would drop blackmail; burned original; Philpot believed reform.
- French accepts story. Notes: Philpot leaves; Roper's knowledge; French suspicion of Philpot dropped.

## Ch 9 The Value of Analysis
- French walks moor, theory: Roper arranged Whymper, Averill's money, murders, fire. Roper "moving spirit" behind Averill's messages. Snag: Mrs Palmer-Gore's invitation.
- French compares Whymper note with Averill samples (from Oxley) — suspects forgery; sends to Yard.
- York: Mrs Palmer-Gore: letter from Averill, asking invite; she thought it cool; never kept letter; didn't know Averill's style.
- Thirsby: Ruth: never knew about flower show until Mrs P-G's letter. Roper/Mrs Roper quarrel: "I'll do you in some day if I swing for it."
- French infers Roper forged letter; Ruth's absence arranged; Simon drugged.

## Ch 10 Whymper Speaks at Last
- French's full theory of Roper: wanted robbery; plan spurred by Mrs Roper hatred; drugged Simon; killed Mrs Roper; burnt house; fail point: Roper's death and money's whereabouts.
- Whymper tells story: Roper's message: Simon's brother Theodore living as Prosper Giraud at Talloires; wrote short stories; Mme Blancquart blackmail; Simon sends £20 and Whymper to go with £500. Theodore's wild life, gambling, cheating, killing; wife's suicide; Ruth left with Simon.
- French bluffs about Ruth's parentage; Whymper gives story; French promises not to use unless necessary.
- Ruth interviewed at Oxleys': father Theodore, Bayonne; mother Anne de Condillac; born Bayonne.
- Biarritz police confirm (5 facts: wine merchant at Bayonne; marriage 24 Jun 1905; Mrs Averill d. 17 Jul 1906 at Ruth's birth; Ruth baptised 19 Aug 1906; Theodore d. 8 Sep 1910, child sent to England).
- Next morning: new idea.

## Ch 11 A Startling Theory
- Sleepless night: idea: Roper faked own death (cf. New York case of fake bodies from cemetery).
- Dr Emerson: bodies not identifiable.
- Body source: hospital (rejected), cemetery (rejected: needs multiple people), murder (third victim). Chief Constable Valentine: no disappearances; murder left no trace.
- French checks Thirsby churchyard, new cemetery, village cemetery (3 miles NE of Starvel). Negative.
- Ruth: Giles died about time of fire; Giles last seen by Ruth Tues, 10 min, Mrs Roper nursing; Dr Philpot's visit Thursday; Giles "tall" (Ruth says no, medium height).
- French infers Giles body used.

## Ch 12 A Somewhat Gruesome Chapter
- Dr Emerson: Giles had myocarditis; certified; coffin. Emerson: only autopsy would prove; he didn't do one.
- Philpot (leaving for Glasgow; address Mrs MacIntosh, 47 Kilgore Street, Dumbarton Road): financial ruin. Gave Giles's records. Giles's influenza, Thursday visit.
- Oxley: Philpot gambler.
- Bloxham at station.
- Exhumation order; Home Office rep Dr Laming; Col. Followes; Kent; policeman. Coffin plate: "Markham Giles, died 14th September, 1926. Aged 36." Coffin empty except ~earth.
- Press: French's story (anonymous letter).
- Undertaker Simkins: Roper ordered coffining Wednesday, funeral Friday, handed £15.

## Ch 13 The Piece of Yellow Clay
- French's reflection: he hopes for promotion; Chief Inspector Armstrong retiring.
- Emerson: says murder unlikely; cocaine/hydrocyanic possible; Roper alone able.
- Giles cottage search: nothing.
- Handcart in outhouse at Starvel; half-moon yellow clay on heel-shaped piece; clay in grave at 3ft depth. French digs; Roper buried loot out on moor.
- Hole found behind house at dusk.

## Ch 14 The Secret of the Moor
- French watches all night in outhouse.
- Morning: Kent and constable dig: blanket-wrapped body: Markham Giles.
- Valentine: inquest. Pullar: heel-shape, size sevens/six-nine.
- Valentine: Dr Lingard to do autopsy. Discussion; Valentine: ruse — French to publicly describe notes, to reassure Roper.
- Inquest adjourned 7 days.

## Ch 15 French Baits His Trap
- Inquest: Emerson; Philpot; Ruth; Mrs Roper's account; undertaker.
- French's public evidence: deliberately mis-states (notes: 10 numbers, reassuring); hint at coffin.
- Dr Lingard: death from cocaine injection; no syringe found; Emerson's error.
- Verdict: wilful murder vs person(s) unknown.
- Valentine: planned (notes, cocaine line).

## Ch 16 A Double Recall
- Roper description (age 34, 5ft 9in, squint, Scottish voice, small hands and feet, stoop).
- French to Kintilloch; Glasgow Philpot (commission agent, new job); Roper's mother in Peebles (huckster's shop).
- Recalled by Chief Inspector Mitchell: two £20 notes passed at Northern Shires Bank (Throgmorton Avenue).
- Willis (Brodrick jewellers case). List of ~200 possibles → 631 replies.

## Ch 17 Concerning Wedding Rings
- Mitchell's story: Whitechapel (Cable St entry): 39 wedding rings on cord; lightermen James Gray (skipper) & William Fuller (crew, cut); tossed from Tower Bridge; Thames lighter *Fickle Jane*; rings found by ferrying.
- Mitchell sends French. Jeweller Alderdice (Strand): 18 carat, 30–35 shillings each.
- French's circular: 40 rings; Monday 6 December; replies to Inspector French, Yard.
- 631 replies, 625 eliminated; six. Shop of Stanley: man with dark moustache (false, fuzzy), tinted glasses, gray Homburg, fawn coat; taxi ~11:30; changed £20 note for 35 shillings. Mr Russell (second shop) confirms: £20 change.

## Ch 18 Cumulative Evidence
- Telegrams: taximen (Marble Arch; Aldwych); Carlton lunch (Tuesday); Peveril Hotel Russell Square (Thursday) as "Jas. Fulton, Manchester."
- Cut on right thumb (7 shop assistants).
- Taxi to Gracechurch Street: Dashwood & Munce (stockbrokers, Dover House). Client "Arthur Lisle Whitman," c/o Andrew Macdonald, 18 Moray Street, Pentland Avenue, Edinburgh (tobacconist). Paid ~£2000 in notes under £10; Brazilian stocks (Govt 5% £1000; rails); Beira Bank at Rio.
- Edinburgh police: Macdonald of shady reputation; letters forwarding.

## Ch 19 The Last Lap
- French's trap: Munce to meet "Whitman" at Waverley 6:15–6:33 pm Tuesday; Munce travels to Aberdeen 10:0 am from King's Cross. Telegram (Dashwood & Munce) "Serious fall in Brazilian stocks impending"; letter confirmation. Whitman replies: "Will meet Munce as suggested."
- Philpot (Glasgow) agrees to identify ("Will meet you place and time stated").
- Inspector Tanner (lookalike) impersonates Munce.
- French travels Monday night (11:35 pm Euston), Edinburgh 8 am Tuesday. Meets Philpot under Scott's Monument at 5 pm.
- Station: Roper absent; train leaves; Tanner retrieves suitcase.
- Refreshment room: Philpot's thumb cut matches; Philpot pulls Mills' bomb pin; struggle; Tanner's jiu-jitsu lock; pin reinserted; handcuffed.

## Ch 20 Conclusion
- Philpot confesses. Cashbox in Glasgow: £36,562 recovered (plus £2000 paid to Dashwood & Munce). Ruth receives fortune; marries Whymper.
- Murder of Edna: silk cord across lower flight (dark-brown); Flora away with Roper; Roper and Flora saw murder from kitchen; Philpot's cricket bat. Roper's blackmail: 40s/week; written confession; Philpot forged confession upside-down; Roper's safe deposit box.
- Starvel plan: Philpot got Simon to employ Ropers; agreed with Roper on murders, fake accident; Roper to emigrate to Brazil.
- Ruth sent to York with forged letter & £10; Simon drugged.
- Giles murdered Tue night, 14 Sep, by cocaine injection (Roper and Philpot together); Roper arranged coffining.
- Whymper episode: Roper kept Simon drugged to get £500.
- Roper faked drunkenness; Mellowes overtook him.
- Night of crime: Philpot strangled Mrs Roper, then Simon, moved money (half each); burned papers; poured petrol; moved Giles's body by handcart; Philpot stabbed Roper in back with knife; buried Giles's body on moor.
- Philpot's fake gambling to disguise money.
- Passport forgery: Arthur Lisle Whitman.
- Philpot executed after trial. Whymper and Ruth married.
